Title: How to Make a Dark Mode Toggle with CSS + localStorage in 10 Lines
Desc: Learn how to build a simple dark mode toggle using CSS and JavaScript with localStorage support so the theme persists across page reloads.
Author: Pro Bandey
Data:
## Dark mode is now a standard feature in modern websites.

Users expect:

```text
Light Mode ↔ Dark Mode
```

The good news?

You can build a working toggle with just a few lines of CSS and JavaScript.

---

## Step 1: Define CSS Variables

We use CSS variables for theme control.

```css id="css-vars"
:root {
  --bg: #ffffff;
  --text: #111111;
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --bg: #111111;
  --text: #ffffff;
}

body {
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--text);
}
```

This allows instant theme switching.

---

## Step 2: Add a Toggle Button

```html id="toggle-btn"
<button id="themeToggle">Toggle Theme</button>
```

Simple UI element.

---

## Step 3: JavaScript Logic (Core)

```js id="theme-js"
const toggle = document.getElementById("themeToggle");
const root = document.documentElement;

// Load saved theme
const saved = localStorage.getItem("theme");
if (saved) root.setAttribute("data-theme", saved);

// Toggle theme
toggle.addEventListener("click", () => {
  const current = root.getAttribute("data-theme");
  const next = current === "dark" ? "" : "dark";

  root.setAttribute("data-theme", next);
  localStorage.setItem("theme", next);
});
```

---

## How It Works

Flow:

```text id="flow"
User Clicks Button
↓
Theme Changes
↓
Saved In localStorage
↓
Reload Page
↓
Theme Restored
```

## Why This Approach Works

### 1. CSS Variables

They make theme switching instant.

---

### 2. data-theme Attribute

Clean way to switch global styles.

---

### 3. localStorage

Persists user preference across sessions.

---

## Common Improvements

### Respect System Theme

You can detect system preference:

```js id="system-theme"
window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")
```

---

### Smooth Transitions

Add this:

```css id="transition"
body {
  transition: background 0.3s, color 0.3s;
}
```

---

### Better Accessibility

Always ensure contrast is readable in both themes.

---

## Common Mistakes

### Hardcoding Colors

Bad:

```css id="bad"
body {
  background: white;
  color: black;
}
```

This breaks theme switching.

---

### Not Saving Preference

Without localStorage, users lose their theme on refresh.

---

### Inconsistent Variables

Always use variables across components.

---

## Real-World Use Cases

Dark mode is used in:

* SaaS dashboards
* Developer tools
* Documentation sites
* Mobile-first web apps

It improves:

* User comfort
* Battery usage (on OLED screens)
* Visual accessibility

---

## FAQ

### Is dark mode hard to implement?

No. With CSS variables and a small JS snippet, it’s simple.

### Why use localStorage?

To remember user preference after page reload.

### Can I auto-detect system theme?

Yes, using `prefers-color-scheme`.

### Is dark mode necessary?

Not required, but expected in modern UI.

### Does it improve UX?

Yes, especially for long usage sessions.

---

## Final Thoughts

Dark mode is one of the easiest but most impactful UI features you can add.

```text id="final-flow"
Define Variables
↓
Toggle Theme
↓
Save Preference
↓
Restore On Load
```

With just a few lines of code, you improve both usability and modern UI expectations.
